subject: Renewal options: commit shift + one-time credit proposal
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Kyle Jensen <kyle@voltix.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal options: commit shift + one-time credit proposal

Hi Kyle —

Thanks again for walking through usage trends last week. Based on the last 12 months and your expected Q2 burst, I pulled together two practical options to keep your unit economics steady while smoothing your spend:

1) 12-month renewal with a 10% list discount + a one-time $50k service credit applied in month 1 (helps offset migration/testing).
2) 18-month renewal with a 7% list discount + ability to shift up to 30% of committed spend between quarters (no change in per-token rate), plus a price hold for 6 months on the core rtx-quant model.

Both options include the same SLA and access to Dedicated capacity during business hours; we can add burst buffer credits as an add-on if you expect spikes. I attached a pricing worksheet and an updated SOW (Voltix_SOW_v3.pdf) for option comparison.

Can you confirm which direction you want to take? If procurement needs a numeric discount approval, I can route to my manager for a signed exception.

Best,
Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: renewal-pricing-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet with scenario comparisons)
From: Kyle Jensen <kyle@voltix.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine.procurement@voltix.com>, Alison Reed <alison@voltix.com>
Date: 2027-02-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options: commit shift + one-time credit proposal

Kim —

Appreciate the clear options. Elaine is copied for procurement alignment. Quick thoughts:
- Option 1 looks attractive if we can move the credit to be refundable against overage in Q1.
- Option 2 is interesting given our seasonal burst, but the 7% discount still leaves us ~15% above our internal target.

Procurement will want to see an alternative that hits closer to the target without extending commitment length too much. Can you do a middle path: 12-month term, 12% discount, $35k credit, and a 3-month price hold instead of 6? If not, we need pricing flexibility tied to committed tokens rather than months.

Also can you send the SKU-level rates (per-token) for the rtx-quant vs standard-quant models — Elaine will need that for the PO.

Thanks,
Kyle
Head of Platform Engineering
Voltix Systems
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Kyle Jensen <kyle@voltix.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-18T13:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options: commit shift + one-time credit proposal

Kyle —

Thanks — yes, I can scope a counter. Rishi, looping you in for pricing approval; Marissa I bumped this because Voltix is asking for a tighter discount tied to a shorter term.

Proposed counter (pre-approval):
- 12 months
- 12% list discount
- $40k one-time credit applied against month 1 invoice (can be applied to overages if you prefer; note: refundable credits require a different contract clause)
- 3-month price hold on rtx-quant model (we can document the hold window in the SOW)

Rishi — can you confirm we can approve 12% + $40k credit? If not, what floor do we have for a 12-month commit? I pasted the pricing sheet into the email thread and also attached the SOW (Voltix_SOW_v3.pdf).

Next steps: if approved, I'll provide a tracked change SOW and a DocuSign link for signatures.

Best,
Kim
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-19T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options: commit shift + one-time credit proposal

Kim / Marissa —

I reviewed Voltix usage and our margin on the rtx-quant family. We can authorize up to 12% on a 12-month term with a maximum one-time credit of $40k, provided the credit is non-refundable (applied to the first invoice and to be consumed against usage). I want to avoid tying credits to refunds — it complicates revenue recognition.

If procurement insists on refundable credits, we could offer a $25k refundable credit but only with a 24-month term. Otherwise, the non-refundable $40k on 12 months is fine. Kim — proceed with the tracked SOW and send DocuSign when ready. Marissa, please let me know if you want to add an executive discount or approve as-is.

Rishi
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Park <elaine.procurement@voltix.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Kyle Jensen <kyle@voltix.com>
Date: 2027-02-19T12:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options: commit shift + one-time credit proposal

Thanks for the options and the quick turnaround. A few procurement points:
- We prefer credit to be refundable against overages for our budgeting. If Redwood will not accept refundable credits on 12 months, we can stretch to 24 months but need the discount to stay >=10%.
- Please provide the SKU per-token rates and a simple PO-ready cost table (line items: committed tokens, expected overage rate, one-time credit line).

If we get the PO-ready table and DocuSign with tracked SOW changes, we can move to internal approvals this week.

Regards,
Elaine Park
Procurement Manager, Voltix Systems
Attachment: Voltix_PO_Template.xlsx (requested PO template placeholder)

Subject: Re: Renewal options: commit shift + one-time credit proposal

Elaine / Kyle —

Thanks — attached is a PO-ready table (renewal-pricing-sheet.xlsx) with per-SKU rates for rtx-quant and standard-quant and two plumbing options:
A) 12-month term / 12% discount / $40k non-refundable credit / 3-month price hold
B) 24-month term / 10% discount / $25k refundable credit / 6-month price hold

Rishi has authorized option A per the thread; option B is available if you prefer refundable credit but requires 24 months. I also created a DocuSign envelope for option A so you can e-sign the SOW quickly: https://www.docusign.com/en/voltx/contract/VLTX-2027-RENEW

If you confirm option A, we'll send the tracked SOW and DocuSign. Quick win is to sign and we’ll provision the Dedicated burst buffer capacity next week.

Thanks,
Kim
